newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-MEXICO SEND SECOND-STRING SQUAD TO COPA AMERICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICO SEND SECOND-STRING SQUAD TO COPA AMERICA.

text.p: Mexico joined the list of countries who have decided to send second-string outfits to this month's Copa America on Thursday.
Mexico followed the examples of Peru, Argentina and Ecuador who are sending what are effectively 'B' teams to the tournament in Bolivia. Colombia will also be without some of their top players.

The Copa America is paying the price for a decision by the organisers to cram it in between the marathon World Cup qualifying competitions being held in the Americas. All countries have given the World Cup full priority.
Many countries have decided their top players need a rest rather than another three weeks of football, some of which will be played at high altitude in the Andean country.
World champions Brazil are one of the few sending a full- strength squad as they qualify automatically for the World Cup in France next year.
Top Mexican players such as strikers Carlos Hermosillo, Zague and Luis Garcia and midfielders Alberto Garcia Aspe and Benjamin Galindo will all be absent in Bolivia.
Coach Bora Milutinovic said: "We have to think of our younger players. If we don't give them a chance in an official competition now, when will we?"
Mexico, who lead the final stage of the CONCACAF qualifying competition face a tough match away to El Salvador on Sunday, just three days before the Copa America begins.
Mexico, along with Costa Rica, have been invited to join the ten South American nations in the Copa America.
It is the third time they have been invited. On the first occasion in 1993 they reached the final where they lost 2-1 to Argentina but last time they were knocked out by the United States.
Goalkeepers: Hugo Pineda (America), Adolfo Rios (Veracruz), Martin Zuniga (Guadalajara)

Defenders: Pavel Pardo (Atlas), Duilio Davino (UAG), Joel Sanchez (Guadalajara), Claudio Suarez (Guadalajara), Camilo Romero (Guadalajara), Javier Savedra (Toros Neza), Francisco de Anda (Santos Laguna)
Midfielders: Paulo Cesar Chavez (Guadalajara), Rodrigo Lara (America), Antonio Sancho (UNAM), Nicolas Ramirez (Santos Laguna), Gilberto Jimenez (Puebla), German Villa (America)
Forwards: Rafael Garcia (UNAM), Jose Manuel Abundis (Toluca), Francisco Palencia (Cruz Azul), Eustacio Rizo (UNAM), Cuauhtemoc Blanco (America), Luis Hernandez (Necaxa)
